title: Event Loop and I/O Knowledge Check
description: Check your understanding of asynchronous execution, event loop phases, blocking work, timers, and worker threads.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: Why can CPU-heavy synchronous work be harmful in a Node.js server?

options.text: It can block the event loop and delay other requests

questions.explanation: JavaScript execution runs on the main thread, so long synchronous work can delay other callbacks and requests.

questions.prompt: Which API is best suited for moving CPU-bound JavaScript work off the main thread?
questions.explanation: Worker threads allow CPU-heavy JavaScript tasks to run outside the main event loop thread.

questions.prompt: What is non-blocking I/O designed to avoid?

options.text: Waiting synchronously while an external operation completes

questions.explanation: Non-blocking I/O lets Node continue handling other work while file, network, or database operations are pending.

questions.prompt: Which callback queue is associated with `setTimeout()`?
questions.explanation: `setTimeout()` callbacks are handled through the event loop's timers phase.
